issues.description: TTS v3 default speaker disagrees with itself: docs say 'aditya', config says 'shubh'
issues.detail: The module docstring, README table, and class docstring all state the v3-beta default speaker is 'aditya', but TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker='shubh'. Same fact (the default identity) is represented in two places that disagree. Pick one source of truth (the config dict) and let the docs read from it, or at minimum reconcile.

issues.description: Speaker is a value but never validated against the model's allowed set
issues.detail: SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums and config.speakers exist precisely to make 'which voices belong to which model' an explicit value. Then __init__ accepts voice_id: Optional[str] and never checks membership. The data is there; the check isn't wired. Either validate at construction or stop pretending the enums constrain anything.

issues.description: Pydantic Field bounds and per-model pace_range complect two different constraints in the same value
issues.detail: pace is declared ge=0.3, le=3.0 at the Pydantic layer, then re-validated and silently clamped against per-model pace_range in __init__. A v3 user passing pace=2.5 passes Pydantic, then gets silently clamped to 2.0 with a warning. The valid range is a function of the model; bind it there, not in two contradicting places.

issues.description: Detecting 'user passed a non-default value' by comparing to the default value is broken sentinel logic
issues.detail: Warnings like 'pitch is ignored for {model}' fire only when params.pitch != 0.0. A user explicitly passing pitch=0.0 to a v3 model gets no warning; a user who never set it but whose default differs gets a spurious one. Identity of 'did the caller specify this?' is being inferred from value equality. Use model_fields_set or an explicit sentinel.

issues.description: MODEL_CONFIGS is the right move; both files would benefit from one shared loader
issues.detail: STT's ModelConfig and TTS's TTSModelConfig are the cleanest part of this PR: capability becomes data, not branching on substring matches of model names. Good. The remaining incidental complexity is that get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models, hiding a typo as a quiet wrong answer. Raise instead.

issues.description: set_prompt's silent no-op when the model doesn't support prompts hides user intent
issues.detail: If prompt is None and the model doesn't support prompts, set_prompt returns silently. That conflates 'this model can't do it' with 'you asked for nothing'. The caller has expressed an intent ('clear the prompt') against a model where the concept doesn't exist; logging at debug or raising would be more honest than a no-op.

review.summary: The PR's central move — replacing substring matches on model names ('saaras' in model.lower()) with a ModelConfig data table — is the right kind of decomposition: model capability becomes a value you look up, not behavior tangled across branches. That's genuinely simpler. What remains complected is the parameter validation story: pace bounds live in Pydantic Field constraints AND in per-model pace_range AND in a silent clamp; 'did the user pass this' is inferred from value equality with defaults; speaker enums exist but voice_id is never validated against them; and the v3 default speaker disagrees with its own docs. The data model is most of the way there — finish pushing the constraints into the config table and stop letting the Pydantic layer make promises it can't keep per-model.
